sources: Al Jazeera liveblog, Hadeel Al Yamani reporting from Taiz, Yemen; local authorities, tribal elders, community figures
fault_line: Is Taiz the next city to fall in Yemen's reopened war, or can government forces hold a siege from three directions?

sections.what_happened: Front lines around Taiz that had been relatively quiet have resumed fighting, with fierce clashes on the western front (Al-Dabab, Jabal Han area and other southwestern locations) as Ansar Allah fighters attempt to break through and advance toward the city to capture it, while government forces try to stop the attack. The eastern front has seen intense attacks for several days, with government forces supported by Popular Resistance fighters pushing back. The city is besieged from several directions (northeast, northwest, southern entrance); the southern front is active with residential neighbourhoods under repeated attack, including Jabal Sabir (southern gateway) and villages outside the city such as Kahlan. Local authorities, tribal elders and community figures warn the Ansar Allah against involving children in areas recently taken in the Taiz region, accusing the group of forcibly recruiting children. BOUNDARY NOTE: this entry is timestamped 01:00 GMT = 05:00 , the scan's closing minute; it is recorded here as a supplement so the next scan dedupes against it rather than re-reporting it.
sections.what_verified: 1 distinct publisher family: Al Jazeera (T2, STATE QA). Context support only (not counted): the Yemeni government 700+ operations claim recorded at totw-20261025-0200-05 is the same offensive's government-side framing.
sections.what_disputed: No Ansar Allah response or independent verification of the capture attempt, casualty figures (none given in the entry) or child-recruitment accusation was carried in the entry. The 700+ operations / 300+ fighters government claim in the same liveblog hour is a single-source battlefield claim, already recorded as such at totw-20261025-0200-05.
sections.why_matters: While the world watches Riyadh's airport, another Yemeni city is under attack from three sides: Ansar Allah fighters are pushing to capture Taiz, and local elders accuse them of forcibly recruiting children in the villages they just took.

totw_analysis: Our read: While the world watches Riyadh's airport, another Yemeni city is under attack from three sides: Ansar Allah fighters are pushing to capture Taiz, and local elders accuse them of forcibly recruiting children in the villages they just took. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Taiz the next city to fall in Yemen's reopened war, or can government forces hold a siege from three directions?
